clue.text: Goddess gives Tom an eye-opener

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, a he-cat

indicators.note: an opener is what starts something, so only the first letter of eye is taken

explanation.surface: A tom cat startles someone with an eye-opening display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' is a male cat, a HE-CAT; 'opener' takes the first letter of 'eye', E.
explanation.definitionFit: Hecate is the Greek goddess of witchcraft, crossroads and the moon.

clue.text: They're bound to open on Sunday !

definitions.text: They're bound to open on Sunday !

parts.words: They're bound to open on Sunday
parts.note: reads as people obliged to start something on a Sunday; really, bound volumes opened at church services each Sunday

explanation.surface: Some people are certain to open for business on Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' means having a book binding, not obliged; these volumes are opened by worshippers at Sunday services.
explanation.definitionFit: Collections of church songs are bound books opened during Sunday worship.

clue.text: Where Arthur was given a beast to mount

parts.note: a camel is a beast of burden

indicators.note: in a down entry, to mount is to climb, so the word to is read upwards

explanation.surface: King Arthur is handed an animal to ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' looks like riding the beast, but in this down clue it turns TO upwards to OT, placed after CAMEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelot is the legendary court and castle of King Arthur.

clue.text: Equivalent to man breaking into a jibe

indicators.note: into signals the scrambled words go inside the other piece

parts.note: a jibe is a taunt, a mocking remark

indicators.note: breaking suggests the words are smashed and reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: A man is described as bursting into a sneering remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges TO MAN into NTAMO, which goes 'into' TAUNT after its TA; the 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantamount to means amounting to the same thing, equal in effect.

clue.text: Last, in spite of everything

definitions.meaning: coming at the end, behind every other one
nevertheless, despite what has been said

explanation.surface: Something comes last despite all that has happened.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both following every other thing and nonetheless, despite all.

clue.text: Conflict about torn materials this time

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fight goes round the other letters

parts.note: a fight is a conflict

indicators.note: the letters of torn are made into new material, a signal to rearrange them

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A dispute over ripped fabric breaks out on this occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'materials' rearranges TORN into ORTN, and FIGHT goes 'about' it; 'this' is a link to the definition 'time'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortnight is a stretch of time lasting two weeks.

clue.text: And so hesitant a dismissal

parts.note: er is the sound a hesitant speaker makes
go is a word of dismissal, telling someone to leave

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly dismisses another person.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, used to introduce a conclusion.

clue.text: Song about people in republic

indicators.note: about means going round, so the song encloses the people

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera
men are people

explanation.surface: A national song about the people of a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ARIA round MEN; 'in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia is a republic in the South Caucasus.

clue.text: They might be torches of course !

definitions.meaning: a link was a torch of pitch and tow carried to light the way in old streets
a golf course by the sea is called the ...

explanation.surface: Things that could serve as torches, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally', but it means belonging to a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means old flaming torches and also a seaside golf course.

clue.text: Game performance

definitions.meaning: a piece performed by one person alone

explanation.surface: A display put on during a game.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a card game, solo whist, and a performance by a single player.

clue.text: It reminds people to follow me

indicators.note: follow means come after, so the people and to are placed after me

parts.note: taken as written
men are people
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gesture urging others to come after the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follow' puts MEN and TO after ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a keepsake that brings a person or event back to mind.

clue.text: Some soldiers don't finish course of treatment

indicators.note: not finishing means the final letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a regiment is a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: Certain soldiers fail to complete their medical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't finish' drops the last letter, T, from REGIMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed plan of diet, exercise or medication.

clue.text: Preparation for the bigger pupils

parts.note: reads as schooling for older children; really, an eye drug that dilates the pupils of the eye

explanation.surface: Getting older schoolchildren ready for the next stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupils' are those of the eye, not schoolchildren: this plant extract was once used to widen them.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly nightshade extract contains atropine, which dilates the eye's pupils.

clue.text: America's responsibility ?

parts.note: reads as a duty of the United States; split as a phrase

explanation.surface: A question about what duty falls to the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: A duty that falls on someone is 'on' them, so America's duty is 'on US'.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or duty resting on someone.

clue.text: Features Manet clumsily showed in wrinkles

indicators.note: showed in means placed inside, so the rearranged letters sit within the wrinkles

parts.note: lines are wrinkles on a face

indicators.note: clumsily suggests the painter's name is put together awkwardly in a new order

explanation.surface: Manet's portrait awkwardly shows facial features in its wrinkles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clumsily' rearranges MANET to AMENT, which is 'showed in' LINES after LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineaments are the distinctive outlines or features of a face.

clue.text: Letters going from the station ?

parts.note: reads as mail leaving a depot; really, mail going out, and a remote station

explanation.surface: Mail being dispatched from a station.
explanation.walkthrough: Outgoing letters are 'out post'; the whole is a remote military station.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a remote station, such as a frontier military camp.

clue.text: A number take part in the game

parts.note: three is a number
some means a part, a portion

explanation.surface: Several people join in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' and 'in the' are links; in golf a match of three players, one against two, has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, a match in which one player plays against two others is so called.

clue.text: Perhaps the sneer of the dour expert

parts.note: grim means dour, stern
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A gloomy specialist's sneering look.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneer is one kind of wry facial contortion, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: King's children, perhaps ?

parts.note: Ethel is a name a child might have
Bert is another name a child might have

explanation.surface: Asking whether these are the offspring of a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'children, perhaps' gives two first names, ETHEL and BERT; ''s' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethelbert was an Anglo-Saxon monarch of Kent, the first English ruler converted to Christianity.

clue.text: Composer is a rent collector

indicators.note: a collector gathers things together, so these letters are gathered into a new order

explanation.surface: A musician moonlights collecting rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collector' rearranges IS A RENT. John Stainer was an English Victorian composer of church music.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Stainer was an English composer, best known for The Crucifixion.

clue.text: Star workers are included

indicators.note: included means held inside, so are goes within the workers

parts.note: worker ants are the classic crossword workers
taken as written

explanation.surface: The star performers are among the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' puts ARE inside ANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Antares is a bright red supergiant star in Scorpius.

clue.text: Generated by the ship passing an East coast feature

definitions.meaning: a passing ship leaves a wake of disturbed water behind it
a large square bay on England's east coast, between Lincolnshire and Norfolk

explanation.surface: Something produced by a passing ship along England's east coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wash is a large bay on England's east coast; a ship's wash is the water it churns up.
explanation.definitionFit: The disturbed water left by a vessel is called its wash, and the Wash is also a bay on England's east coast.

clue.text: Article poet wrote fairly slowly

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
Dante was the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A poet writing at a fairly leisurely pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the musical tempo marking for a moderately slow, walking pace.

clue.text: Some past account of backward animals

indicators.note: backward means the letters taken are read from right to left
some means a part of the words that follow, so letters are taken from within them

explanation.surface: Part of an old report about slow-witted creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes STAC from 'paST ACcount'; 'backward' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats are animals, domestic felines.

clue.text: Wood works in church

indicators.note: in signals the works sit inside the church

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England
ops is short for opera, works

explanation.surface: Wooden fittings are installed in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts OPS inside CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small wood of trees or bushes.

clue.text: Had Lamb ode read out weekly

indicators.note: out means disordered, so these letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone read a poem by Lamb aloud every week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges HAD LAMB ODE; 'read' is a link. Charles Lamb was an English essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebdomadal comes from Greek hebdomas, seven days, meaning occurring every week.

clue.text: The low-down sort of pusher

definitions.meaning: a drug pusher deals in narcotics

explanation.surface: A lowly kind of person who pushes others around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pusher' is a drug dealer, and he sells drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses the word for inside information and for narcotics that a dealer sells.

clue.text: None to climb without direction ? That's right

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the first piece goes round the second
in a down entry, climbing means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: nil means none
E is east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Asking whether nobody climbs without guidance is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to climb' turns NIL up to LIN; 'without' (meaning outside) puts it round E.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid.

clue.text: Left one firm to build the colonnade

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
I is the Roman numeral one
Co is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A single company was left to build a row of columns.
explanation.definitionFit: A portico is a porch with a roof supported by a row of columns.

clue.text: Gives a quarter in cash as expiation

indicators.note: in signals placing the pieces inside the cash

parts.note: pence are cash, coins
N, north, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone hands over a quarter in money to atone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter' gives A and N (north, a compass quarter), and 'in' puts AN inside PENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is an act of self-punishment done to make amends for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Extracts scene-shifter in Oriental vessel

parts.note: E is short for east, the Orient

indicators.note: in places the shifted letters inside the vessel

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: a shifter moves things, so the scene's letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A stagehand is aboard an Eastern ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A scene-shifter is a stagehand; here 'shifter' rearranges SCENE to SENCE, which goes 'in' SS after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Essences are concentrated extracts of plants or flavours.

clue.text: Look for a little gamble with Tim's capital

parts.note: spec is short for speculation, a gamble

indicators.note: capital means the first, capital letter of the word

explanation.surface: Tim's money is used for a small bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money, but it takes the first letter of Tim's, T.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is the appearance or look of something.
